summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 is dominated by the three major hyperscalers — AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, and Google Vertex AI — each offering managed access to foundation models within the customer's own cloud boundary. Data-platform players (Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx) compete by bringing models to where enterprise data already lives, while edge and alternative clouds (Cloudflare Workers AI, Oracle Cloud AI) target latency-sensitive and existing-contract use cases. There is no single winner — selection is driven by existing cloud contracts, data gravity, compliance requirements, and model availability.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy — prompts and completions stay inside the enterprise's own cloud/VPC boundary and are not used to train vendor models, satisfying regulatory and IP-protection requirements.
Compliance and governance — aggregators provide SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR, and FedRAMP coverage plus audit logging, access controls, and content filtering out of the box.

Single billing and existing cloud contracts — consumption is billed through the enterprise's existing cloud agreement (EDP/MACC commitments), avoiding new vendor procurement and leveraging committed-spend discounts.
Unified security and identity — models are accessed through native IAM, private networking, key management, and monitoring that already govern the rest of the cloud estate.

Model choice and portability — a single managed API provides access to many foundation models (Claude, Llama, Gemini, Mistral, etc.), reducing lock-in to any one model vendor and simplifying switching.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (on-demand) plus provisioned throughput for guaranteed capacity; billed through AWS account with committed-spend discounts.
key_features: Knowledge Bases (RAG) and Agents / AgentCore runtime
platforms.best_for: Enterprises standardized on AWS wanting the broadest multi-vendor model catalog (30+ models) with deep AWS-native security.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token on-demand plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; billed via Azure with MACC commitments.
key_features: Foundry agent service and model catalog
platforms.best_for: Enterprises on Microsoft/Azure wanting first-class, exclusive access to the latest OpenAI frontier models with enterprise governance.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token and per-request, plus GSU (Generative Scale Unit) reserved throughput — e.g. 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash yields ~67,250 tokens/sec sustained.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises on Google Cloud wanting Gemini plus third-party models with strong data/ML tooling and predictable reserved throughput.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits; billed through existing Snowflake contract, no separate model vendor billing.
key_features: Runs inside Snowflake data perimeter (no data movement)
RBAC and governance inherited from Snowflake
platforms.best_for: Enterprises whose data gravity is in Snowflake and want LLMs applied directly to governed data without export.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Capacity-unit (RU/token) consumption pricing; available on IBM Cloud, on-premises, or hybrid via Cloud Pak for Data.
key_features: watsonx.governance for model risk and audit
Granite open-source models with IP indemnification
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises needing strong AI governance, hybrid/on-prem control, and vendor indemnification; recognized as a Gartner/IDC leader.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-character/token on-demand plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity; billed via OCI, including sovereign cloud regions.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises on Oracle/OCI (especially Oracle database and ERP customers) needing sovereign regions and dedicated isolated capacity.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Usage-based per neuron/token on Cloudflare's serverless platform; low-cost, no GPU provisioning required.
key_features: AI Gateway for logging, caching, rate limiting
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, globally distributed inference on open models at the edge, often as a model gateway.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: DBU consumption-based pricing plus pay-per-token model serving; billed through existing Databricks/cloud contract.
key_features: Models run within the Lakehouse data perimeter
Mosaic AI Gateway and Agent Framework
platforms.best_for: Enterprises on Databricks Lakehouse wanting unified data, training, fine-tuning, and governed model serving in one platform.
